h: What you get in the morning
x: slowship is a careful reader for everything your project brings aboard. It reads the code of your packages, your coding agent’s skills and MCP servers, and your own build, without running any of it, and tells you which ones do more than they say.
You need Node.js and five minutes. A local model makes slowship sharper, but it works without one.
Go to the project you’re about to ship and type one word. slowship reads everything aboard, then leaves you a verdict and a short list of what to look at.
The report is where you read a watch properly: the verdict, a short queue of what needs you, and the real code behind every finding. It runs on your own computer and answers nothing else.
You don’t have to leave the terminal. After a watch, press ↵ on the verdict card, or run slowship review any time, and the whole review opens full screen.
When you’ve looked at something and you’re happy with it, clear it. It stops asking, until its code changes.

h: Check it or turn it off
x: slowship is meant to be slow. Let it read while you sleep, and the verdict is waiting when you open your laptop.

h: Or set it up in the report
Test it, check it, stop it
x: The verdict, sent to where you’ll see it when you wake: a Discord channel or a Telegram chat. It’s optional and off until you connect one.

h: Why there’s no tool to clear
x: Your coding agent installs packages, skills and MCP servers for you now, usually without reading them. slowship can be what it asks first.
slowship can gate a build: the exit code is 2 when the verdict is held, so a pipeline stops before a package that does more than it says reaches production.
Four kinds of cargo, found in one pass with no setup. Everything is read where it already sits, except MCP servers that live on npm, which are downloaded into quarantine first.

h: What the model does, and doesn’t
x: A funnel that goes from cheap to careful. Most things are settled by plain rules in a blink. Only what’s worth a second opinion goes to the model, and the final word always stays in code.

h: Code that only exists while running
Languages it reads lightly, or not yet
x: slowship reads code; it never runs it. That’s what makes it safe, and it’s also its limit. Here is everything it knows it can miss.

h: It never runs what it reads
Your agent can look, never clear
x: A checker should never be the way something gets in. Everything slowship reads stays in quarantine, nothing it reads is started, and almost nothing ever leaves your computer.
Everything slowship understands, on one page.
Every number slowship quotes was measured, on real code, on one laptop. Here they all are, with what they don’t say.
